title: Bekhorot 59 - Counting Sheep

chapters.title: Rava's Chidush on Automatic Holiness
chapters.about: Rava teaches that the tenth animal becomes holy on its own even without being explicitly named.

chapters.title: Searching for Sources for Rava
chapters.about: Reviewing baraitot about miscounts where the ninth animal is called the tenth.

chapters.title: Contradiction and Rabbi Shimon's Position
chapters.about: Resolving a conflicting baraita through the view of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda regarding uprooting the name ten.

chapters.title: Minyan Haraoi - A Worthy Count
chapters.about: Analyzing Rava's principle that a proper count exempts the animals even if the tenth animal dies.

chapters.title: Scenarios with Multiple Exits
chapters.about: Examining how splitting sheep between different exits impacts the ma'aser count.

summary: Rabbi Hidary goes through Masekhet Bechorot, analyzing the rules of counting animals for ma'aser behemah and when animals automatically become holy. He discusses various baraitot and mishnayot regarding what happens when a counter makes mistakes in the count or when animals die or exit through multiple openings.
questions: Does an animal become holy as a ma'aser automatically even if the owner does not say anything?
What is the status of the ninth animal if the counter mistakenly calls it the tenth?
If an animal designated as the tenth dies in the pen, are the previously counted animals exempt from being counted again?
How does a pen with multiple exits affect the counting of animals for ma'aser behemah?
